newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse closes down, shrugs off Dow gains.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse closes down, shrugs off Dow gains.

text.p: Belgium's Bel-20 leading share index shrugged off Wall Street's opening gains to close lower with dealers expecting the bourse to slow down in coming days as investors leave the market to take their Christmas holidays.
Dealers expect the bourse to see thin trade until New Year.
"It's pretty dead today, there are still some traders around but the bigger clients are on vacation now and they won't make a move before next year," said a trader.
The Bel-20 index closed down 0.15 percent at 1,882.34 with a moderate 1.91 billion francs of Belgian shares traded.
Dealers closely watched electronics firm Barco which saw its first day on the Bel-20 today. It closed down 0.36 percent at 5,480 francs.
But they expected the share to see some selling pressure in coming weeks.
"The price of Barco is too high, it should be around 5,250 to 5,300 francs," said analyst Martine Glineur at broker Mignon, Hanart, Declerck.
She added Barco had risen in anticipation of its Bel-20 introduction today but that the market would now start focusing on its growth potential again.
Analyst Geert De Mesure at Bank Delen said that "certainly in the short term there is pressure on the price as there will be some profit taking".

Steel maker Cockerill Sambre, which moved out of the Bel-20 after closing hours on Friday, rose in Monday trading to close up two francs at 114 francs with 143,588 shares traded. Analysts said the stock was likely to rise in coming weeks as selling pressure had now eased.
Retailer Delhaize saw 122,400 of its shares traded on the back of a legal victory by its U.S. unit Food Lion against ABC television.
Chemicals and drugs firm UCB closed down 0.68 francs at 80,700 francs after touching 82,500 francs during the day, with dealers expecting the stock to reach 100,000 in the coming year.
